security_audit.summary: All 23 static alerts are false positives: the flagged text is documentation, Blender property handling, or viewport settings. The builder clears existing material nodes before validating inputs, so a failed run can leave a shared material altered. No evidence found of prompt injection or data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The builder clears the node tree of any existing material with the requested name before validating inputs.
remediation.suggestion: Use a unique material name by default and require explicit approval to replace an existing material. Build and validate the replacement before modifying the original.

semantic_findings.description: The builder silently clears an existing material's nodes when its name matches the requested name. Every object using that material can be affected, even if the builder later rejects the input.

content.value_statement: Connecting texture maps by hand can introduce color space and channel errors. Build Principled BSDF materials from local maps or presets, and check the setup before export.
actual_capabilities: Detects texture roles from recognized filename suffixes and connects the maps to a Principled BSDF shader.
Sets base color and emission images to sRGB and data maps to Non-Color.
Splits packed ORM maps and routes occlusion to the glTF material output group.
Inverts the green channel of a DirectX normal map in the shader for Blender.
Creates preset materials such as gold, rubber, glass, and ceramic, with an optional sRGB color override.
Sets up alpha or height displacement and assigns the material to named Blender objects.
limitations: Running the builder requires Blender's Python environment.
Texture detection uses filename tokens and takes the first match for each map type.
The builder does not bake procedural textures or run an engine export.
Reusing an existing material name replaces its shader nodes, affecting other objects that share it.

output: The base color image uses sRGB. The ORM and normal images use Non-Color.
ORM red feeds glTF occlusion, green feeds roughness, and blue feeds metallic.
The shader inverts the normal map's green channel. Prepare an OpenGL normal texture for export rather than relying on the shader conversion.

best_practices: Use a unique material name and save to a separate Blender file while testing.
Use sRGB for base color and emission, and Non-Color for roughness, metallic, and normal maps.
Verify the target engine's normal convention and packing layout before export.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse a material name unless you intend to replace its shader nodes.
Do not bake ambient occlusion or shadows into a base color texture.
Do not assume Blender procedural nodes will transfer to a game engine without baking.

faq.question: Can I create a material without texture files?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose a preset such as gold, rubber, or glass. You can override its base color with an sRGB value.

faq.question: What does ORM mean?
faq.answer: ORM packs ambient occlusion into red, roughness into green, and metallic into blue.

faq.question: Can I use a DirectX normal map?
faq.answer: Yes. The builder can invert the green channel in the shader using a recognized suffix or the DirectX normal option. It leaves the image file unchanged.

faq.question: Why was an image skipped?
faq.answer: The builder needs a recognized filename token and uses the first match for each map type. Rename the image or supply the intended files directly.

faq.question: What happens if the material name already exists?
faq.answer: The builder clears and rebuilds that material's shader nodes. Use a unique name to avoid changing other objects that share the material.

faq.question: Does the builder export a glTF file?
faq.answer: No. It sets up shader nodes, including an occlusion connection for glTF. Run the exporter separately and check the result.
